info.title: Kosta API
info.description:
Kosta is a payments backend for wallet apps. It keeps a proper ledger of every naira, cent or penny that moves, so balances are always right, money can never be spent twice, and every change can be traced.

**What it guarantees**

- **Every movement balances.** Money is never created or lost: each transaction takes from one place and puts the same amount somewhere else. The database itself refuses anything that does not add up.
- **No overdrafts, even under heavy load.** When many requests try to spend the same balance at once, only the ones the balance can cover go through.
- **Safe retries.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` with transfers and withdrawals. If the same request arrives twice, say a phone retries after a timeout, the second one gets the original answer and no money moves again.
- **History cannot be rewritten.** Ledger records cannot be edited or deleted. Mistakes are fixed with new, visible correcting entries.
- **Whole numbers only.** Amounts are in the smallest unit (kobo, cents), so there are no rounding errors.
- **Trusted deposits.** Notifications from payment providers must be signed, and the same payment can never be credited twice.
- **A full paper trail.** Every action is logged, and a books check proves everything balances.

**Signing in**

Send your API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Client keys only see the wallets they opened. Admin keys can also review withdrawals, freeze wallets, read the activity log and run the books check.

post.description: Moves money from one of your wallets to any other wallet in the same currency. Both sides change together or not at all, so money is never lost halfway. If the sender does not have enough, nothing moves and you get insufficient_funds. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request never pays twice.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: A unique key you choose for this payment (a UUID works well). If the same request is sent again with the same key, you get the original response back and no money moves twice. On this docs page, leave it as `new-key-per-click` and a fresh key is made each time you press Execute. Type your own key and press Execute twice to see the replay.

currency.description: Three-letter currency code, like NGN or USD.

schema.description: Done. The money has moved.

422.description: The request was understood but breaks a money rule.

schema.description: The request was understood but breaks a money rule.

code.description:
One of:
- `insufficient_funds`: the wallet cannot cover the amount (plus the fee, for withdrawals).
- `currency_mismatch`: the two wallets hold different currencies.
- `same_account`: you try to send money to the same wallet.
- `idempotency_key_reused`: a key you already used is sent again with a different body.
- `constraint_violation`: a database safety check stopped the change (a last line of defence that should never trigger).

examples: The account does not have enough available balance.

post.summary: Payment received (called by your payment provider)
post.description:
Your payment provider (Paystack, Flutterwave and so on) calls this when a customer pays in, and Kosta credits their wallet. You do not call it yourself; on this docs page, use the Sandbox deposit instead.

How it stays safe:

- Every call must be signed with a secret only you and the provider know, sent in `X-Kosta-Signature`.
- Calls older than 5 minutes are refused, so a captured request cannot be replayed later.
- Providers often send the same notification more than once. Each payment is credited exactly once.
- Kosta answers 200 to every properly signed call so the provider stops retrying, and records any that could not be applied for the team to review.

id.description: The provider's id for this notification.

type.description: Only deposit.succeeded moves money. Other types are acknowledged and ignored.

amount.description: Amount in the smallest unit of the currency (kobo for NGN, cents for USD). So 150000 means NGN 1,500.00. Whole numbers only.

currency.description: Three-letter currency code, like NGN or USD.

200.description: Received. The status says what happened.

status.description: processed: wallet credited. duplicate: already credited before, nothing changed. ignored: not a deposit. failed: could not be applied (see reason).

schema.description: Received. The status says what happened.

get.description: An on-demand audit of the whole ledger. It confirms that money in and money out match exactly in every currency, that every wallet balance agrees with its full history, and that no transaction is lopsided. It also shows how much is owed to customers, how much is on hold for withdrawals and how much has been earned in fees. If anything is off, ok is false and the problem is listed.

settlement.description: Mirror of the money at the bank (negative means held for customers).

withdrawals_pending.description: On hold for withdrawals awaiting review.

mismatched_accounts.description: Wallets whose balance disagrees with their history. Empty when all is well.

unbalanced_entries.description: Transactions that do not add up. Empty when all is well.

schema.description: The reconciliation report.
